source_citation: ICAR-IIRR Rice Water Management Manual (2020); FAO-56 (1998)
agronomic_usage_specification: 800 mm represents the minimum seasonal water for viable rainfed puddled rice. Must NEVER be compared with raw rainfall under irrigated management (e.g. Punjab irrigated rice with 450 mm rain). Under rainfed regime, rainfall < 800 mm applies Tier 2 Liebig soft penalty, NOT Tier 1 hard exclusion.

250-350 mm represents total consumptive water (ETc) across the winter cycle. Winter rainfall in NW plains is only 40-100 mm; comparing raw rainfall to ETc would falsely exclude wheat from India's primary wheat bowl. Used strictly in Tier 2 water scoring.
400-550 mm is seasonal ETc. Under rainfed conditions, rainfall < 400 mm causes stress during silking; evaluated as Tier 2 Liebig penalty, NOT Tier 1 hard exclusion.

production_system: Rainfed Deep Vertisols / Irrigated Northern Plains
agronomic_usage_specification: 500 mm is the minimum rainfed seasonal precipitation for commercial boll setting in central vertisols. In northern irrigated zones (Punjab/Haryana), rainfall is 250 mm and irrigation supplies the balance. Hard exclusion on raw rainfall prohibited.
1200-1800 mm represents total ETc across 12-18 months. Sugarcane in Maharashtra receives 500 mm rain and 1300 mm irrigation. Raw rain comparison prohibited.
450-550 mm is seasonal ETc. In rainfed vertisols, stored soil moisture buffers dry spells; rainfall < 450 mm reduces yield but does not cause 100% death.
400 mm is rainfed screening threshold. In summer groundnut (Gujarat/AP), crop is grown under 100% assured irrigation with zero rain. Raw rain comparison prohibited.
300-450 mm represents ETc. In plains, winter rain is 30-60 mm; crop requires 4-6 light furrow irrigations. Comparing raw rainfall to ETc is invalid.
200-300 mm is seasonal ETc. Winter rain in central India is 20-50 mm; crop relies heavily on deep vertisol profile moisture. Evaluating raw rain against ETc is invalid.
200-280 mm is seasonal ETc. Relies on post-rice residual soil moisture. Comparing raw rain to ETc is invalid.
200-350 mm is seasonal ETc. Winter rainfall in Rajasthan is 20-40 mm; mustard produces record yields with 2 canal irrigations. Comparing raw rain to ETc is invalid.
400-600 mm is seasonal ETc. Commercial hybrid tomato requires frequent light irrigation. Comparing raw rainfall to ETc is invalid.
350-500 mm is seasonal ETc. Shallow root system requires uniform irrigation; raw rain comparison prohibited.
1400-2000 mm is annual ETc. Jalgaon banana belt receives 650 mm rain and 1400 mm drip irrigation. Raw rain comparison prohibited.
300 mm is protective establishment water for young grafts. Mature orchard trees tap deep subsoil groundwater and require winter dry rest for floral induction. Raw rain comparison prohibited.
350 mm is rainfed production screening threshold for economic grain setting. Under rainfed conditions, rainfall < 350 mm reduces yield; evaluated as Tier 2 soft penalty.
350-500 mm is seasonal ETc. Deep taproot extracts moisture up to 1.5 m depth. Raw rain comparison prohibited.
200-300 mm is seasonal ETc. Highly drought resistant; raw rain comparison prohibited.

source_citation: ICAR-AICRP-PM Pearl Millet Production Manual (2020); FAO-56 (1998)
agronomic_usage_specification: 200 mm is rainfed screening threshold for grain development. Exceptional drought tolerance (C4 photosynthetic pathway). In hyper-arid rainfed conditions, evaluated via Tier 2 soft scoring.
